doc.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023

title: Tom Scott on the horn section and the icing on the cake
summary: Rowe reads Tom Scott's account of the Partridge Family horn section; Findley agrees and describes decorating records and thanking clients.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: I’m going to share another thing from — here’s what Tom Scott had to say about that question. And he said that he did some sessions with a producer that did The Partridge Family and David Cassidy records. And he said, “The horn section at that time was me, Chuck Findley, Ollie Mitchell, Slyde Hyde and Lou McCurry. So even if the tune was kind of dumb or mundane it didn’t matter. We were there to play the best damn horn section you’ve ever heard in your life. We took our part very seriously. We didn’t know how far in the mix it was going to be or whether it was going to be there at all. Our job was to go in there and play with one another which we took great joy in doing. Whatever the music is, man, we’ll nail it. So that was soul gratifying just to do that, regardless of the artist.”

We did that all the time. And actually Mike Melvoin wrote all those charts for that particular album. But we always, one thing I always did, always did after a session, whether it was good or bad I mean the track. I’m not talking about what we did but I’m just, like Tom said, we would make the record. We were like the icing on the cake you know. You know you build a house but you need to decorate it. We decorated it. We decorated all kinds of things you know and make it sellable, this house. You know? Because it didn’t look very good without any decoration, without it being painted or furnished or, you know, everything else that makes a house beautiful. Same thing with like a cake and you put the icing on it. And that’s what we did. And but I would always say thank you and good luck with your project. Always. Because I want to thank them for the gig and I also wanted to thank them and hope that they did well on their project because there were many, many records that were not really necessarily a great song or anything but we made magic on those songs. And they did make money off it. And they did have a hit. If you heard the basic tracks without the horns, without us on it, then huh, what can I say? I mean you could listen to them and a lot of them are great, a lot of them aren’t great. © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-
